analysis.investment_thesis: Lloyds Engineering is riding genuine tailwinds in India's capital goods and infrastructure cycle — revenue has compounded 157% over 3 years from a tiny base — but at 48x P/E with sub-10% ROCE and a promoter holding below 50%, the price already bakes in perfection for a business that is still proving its execution at scale.
key_strengths: Explosive revenue ramp: ₹50 Cr → ₹846 Cr in 3 years (157% CAGR), with net profit growing even faster at 160% CAGR
Clean balance sheet: D/E of only 0.16 and ₹95 Cr cash, well within my Debt/Equity comfort zone
Sector positioned at intersection of Make in India, energy transition, and steel/hydrocarbon capex — structural multi-year tailwind
key_risks: P/E of 48x is nearly double my ceiling for capital goods; EV/EBITDA of 47x prices in flawless execution for years — leaves no margin of safety
ROCE of only 9.8% is sub-cost-of-capital for an industrial EPC business; high gross margins (24%) are not converting to efficient capital deployment
Promoter stake at 41.92% — below my preferred 50% floor — and equity nearly tripled in FY25 (₹411 Cr → ₹1,188 Cr), suggesting a large dilutive equity raise
red_flags: OCF positive in only 1 of last 4 years — EPC working capital cycles are brutal; FY25 positive OCF (₹158 Cr) must sustain before trusting the earnings quality
Massive balance sheet expansion in FY25 (total assets ₹571 Cr → ₹1,845 Cr) without sufficient explanation — likely a large QIP diluting existing shareholders
Finance costs tripling YoY (₹3 Cr → ₹9 Cr) while ROCE stays below 10% — warns of capital misallocation risk as the order book scales
analysis.detailed_analysis:
Lloyds Engineering is a genuine India manufacturing story — specialty capital equipment for refineries, steel plants, ports, and power plants, exactly where government capex is flowing. The top-line sprint from ₹50 Cr to ₹846 Cr in three years is real, driven by a booming order book in process equipment and EPC contracts. Operating margins have held above 17%, which is respectable for this segment, and the near-zero leverage (D/E 0.16) means the balance sheet is not a near-term risk. The FY25 FCF turning positive at ₹92 Cr for the first time is an important milestone that deserves monitoring.

However, as a value-conscious investor, I cannot ignore the price being paid here. At 48x P/E and 47.6x EV/EBITDA, the market is valuing this as a premium software-like compounder, not an industrial fabricator with lumpy EPC revenues and thin working capital discipline. ROCE of 9.8% is the single most damning number — a business earning less than its cost of capital destroys value regardless of the top-line narrative. The promoter's stake slipping to 41.92% via what appears to be a large equity raise in FY25 further diminishes the alignment I demand. I would need the price to correct to sub-25x earnings before this becomes a serious allocation — today, wait and watch.
